expectations.text: The first message welcomes the shopper and tells them they can type their own answer and can stop the questions at any time, before any question is asked.
expectations.evidence: Turn 1 opens with the welcome including 'you can always type your own answer' and 'just say "that's enough"', then asks. The welcome rides in the same message as questions 1 and 2 rather than standing alone.

expectations.text: No single message to the shopper contains more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: Turn 4 asks three: budget, washing, and where to shop. This is exactly how Step 1 lays out turn four when the store is not already evident, so the skill's own layout breaks its own rule.

expectations.text: The question about how many pieces they want is asked before the question about budget.
expectations.evidence: Count is asked in turn 2, budget in turn 4.

expectations.text: All nine opening brief questions are asked before any specific garment is named or shortlisted.
expectations.evidence: Brief completes by turn 4. No garment is named anywhere in the transcript; the run stops at the store.

expectations.text: Height, rise, leg width and waist style are all asked before any specific garment is named or shortlisted.
expectations.evidence: Height and rise in turn 5, leg width and waist style in turn 6, both before the store is opened.

expectations.text: Colour and pattern are both asked before any specific garment is named or shortlisted.
The brief is read back to the shopper in a single summary line before shopping begins.
expectations.evidence: Read back twice, once mid-brief and once in the final turn before opening the store.
